newsitem.title: INDIA: Police kill seven guerrillas in southern India.
newsitem.headline: Police kill seven guerrillas in southern India.

text.p: Seven Maoist guerrillas were killed in a shoot-out with police on Friday in the southern Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, police said.
The shoot-out between the guerrillas of the outlawed People's War Group (PWG) and the police took place near the Laxmapur forest, about 70 km (44 miles) from Hyderabad, the state capital.
In another incident, the Maoist guerrillas shot dead a political worker of the ruling Telugu Desam party in Nizamabad district of the state, the Press Trust of India news agency said.
The PWG is one of many Maoist rebel groups considered part of the Naxalite movement, which started in India in the 1960s among groups which split from the main communist party.
It was first banned in Andhra Pradesh in 1992 but gained a year-long reprieve beginning in June 1995 before being banned again in July last year.
